```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 2.6)
library(mssrscopR)
show <- function(m, main) {
  graphics::image(t(m[nrow(m):1, ]), col = grDevices::gray.colors(128, 0, 1),
                  axes = FALSE, main = main, cex.main = 0.9, asp = nrow(m) / ncol(m))
}
```

All images here are synthetic and generated in this document, so the true
scene is known.

## The operator

Mean-Shift Super-Resolution (MSSR; Torres-García et al. 2022,
doi:10.1038/s41467-022-34693-9) subtracts a local, range-weighted mean-shift
estimate from each pixel and refines the result over `order` steps. `fwhm` is
the point-spread-function width in **input pixels** and has no default.

```{r points}
g <- expand.grid(r = 1:31, c = 1:41)
spot <- function(r0, c0, a = 1) a * exp(-((g$r - r0)^2 + (g$c - c0)^2) / (2 * (3 / 2.3548)^2))
pair <- function(sep) matrix(spot(16, 18) + spot(16, 18 + sep) + 0.05, 31, 41)
x <- pair(3)                       # two sources 3 px apart, FWHM 3 px
res <- mssr(x, fwhm = 3, amp = 2)
res
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
show(x, "input"); show(as.matrix(res), "mssr(amp = 2)")
par(op)
```

The amplified grid only adds samples. `mssr_coords()` places them in
input-pixel units, and the field of view stays `[0.5, n + 0.5]`:

```{r coords}
range(mssr_coords(res)$col)
res$transform$spacing
```

How far does the separation go? Compare the value at the midpoint between the
two sources with the value at a source center, in the input and in the MSSR
map (values below 1 mean a dip between the sources):

```{r separation}
mid_ratio <- function(sep) {
  x <- pair(sep)
  r <- mssr(x, fwhm = 3, amp = 2)
  v <- as.matrix(r)
  co <- mssr_coords(r)
  row <- which.min(abs(co$row - 16))
  at_input <- function(cc) stats::approx(1:41, x[16, ], cc)$y
  at_mssr <- function(cc) stats::approx(co$col, v[row, ], cc)$y
  c(input = at_input(18 + sep / 2) / at_input(18), mssr = at_mssr(18 + sep / 2) / at_mssr(18))
}
round(rbind(`2.4 px` = mid_ratio(2.4), `3 px` = mid_ratio(3)), 3)
```

At 3 px the input shows only a shallow dip, which MSSR deepens strongly. At
2.4 px the blurred sources form a single hump, and MSSR returns a single,
sharper hump: it enhances existing structure but does not split sources that
the blur has already merged.

## Known failure modes

MSSR is nonlinear. A dim structure next to a bright one is strongly
suppressed, and broad filled objects can be hollowed or fragmented:

```{r failures}
y <- matrix(spot(16, 14) + spot(16, 21.5, 0.1) + 0.02, 31, 41)   # 10:1 brightness
disk <- outer(1:31, 1:41, function(r, c) as.numeric((r - 16)^2 + (c - 21)^2 <= 81))
disk <- disk + 0.02
ry <- as.matrix(mssr(y, fwhm = 3))
rd <- as.matrix(mssr(disk, fwhm = 3))
c(input_ratio = y[16, 22] / y[16, 14], mssr_ratio = ry[16, 22] / ry[16, 14])
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
show(ry, "dim beside bright"); show(disk, "filled disk"); show(rd, "mssr(disk)")
par(op)
```

The outputs are therefore **not quantitative**; `res$diagnostics$quantitative`
is always `FALSE`.

## Masks with measurements on the original data

A structure map can select pixels, but measurements belong to the original
image. `mssr_mask()` keeps an exact number of pixels of a region.
`tie_fraction` reports the share of the selected pixels that random
tie-breaking decided. That share can be large, because the mean shift is
clipped at zero and many pixels tie there.

```{r mask}
m <- mssr_mask(mssr(x, fwhm = 3), fraction = 0.2)
c(coverage = attr(m, "coverage"), tie_fraction = attr(m, "tie_fraction"))
c(mean_all = mean(x), mean_masked = mean(x[m]))
```

Selecting pixels this way changes the measured population. It is not known to
improve any downstream analysis, so evaluate it for your own task.

## Degenerate input and unsupported requests

Flat frames return zeros flagged as degenerate. Requests the package cannot
honor fail with classed errors:

```{r errors}
mssr(matrix(1, 5, 5), fwhm = 3)$diagnostics[c("degenerate", "degenerate_reason")]
try(mssr(array(0, c(4, 4, 3)), fwhm = 3))     # no axis is guessed
try(mssr(matrix(c(1, NA, 3, 4), 2), fwhm = 3)) # non-finite input
```

## Checking an installation

`mssr_selftest()` recomputes the bundled synthetic fixtures. They were produced
by the accepted engine definition, so this is a regression check of the
installation, not an independent validation:

```{r selftest}
st <- mssr_selftest()
st[, c("fixture_id", "max_abs_error", "passed")]
```
